analyst_view.overall: Second-tier Torreense (19th, 6 pts) host Celtic (32nd, 3 pts) in Leiria, because their own small ground does not meet UEFA rules. Under new coach Joao Nuno, Torreense beat Ararat 3-2 with ten men last time in Europe, but scorer Jorge Aguirre is banned (counted, -8% on their goals) and Baradji and Jatta are injured. Martin O'Neill's Celtic are on three straight league wins, but Mika Baur and Alistair Johnston are out (both counted), and Benjamin Nygren's heel problem now looks likely to keep him out: two Celtic news sites report his absence from the trip, though I could only confirm the doubt in full articles. Tierney is back at left-back and Trusty back in the squad. Dutch referee Allard Lindhout, who shows few cards (about 3.3 a game), is in charge, and Celtic play again in the league three days later.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and already take about 19% off Celtic for Baur and 8% off Torreense for Aguirre's ban. Nygren, one of Celtic's main attackers, is not on their list and now looks set to miss out, so I cut a bit more than before, to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, already up about 7% for Celtic's recent corner count and Torreense conceding many. Celtic should have most of the ball with or without Nygren, so I stay at 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.9 cards, already cut by about 25% for referee Allard Lindhout's low card record (3.3 a game in 61 games). Torreense finished their last European game with ten men and Mutombo is one yellow from a ban, but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, already up for Celtic's recent shooting and Torreense allowing many shots lately. Without Nygren, Celtic lose one of their busiest shooters, which the numbers do not know, so I trim slightly, to about 26.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Without Baur (counted) and very likely Nygren (not counted), Celtic lose two of their sharper shooters, so I go lower, to about 8.5.
